deduplication: OS-package results only; group by advisory ID, retain distinct package-name/installed-version/target tuples. Separate CVE IDs remain separate even when fixes overlap.
acceptance: No risk acceptance or scanner exception is granted by this analysis.

assessment.exploit_condition: infocmp analyzes crafted terminfo data.
assessment.assessment: ncurses-bin is installed, but KMP has no infocmp/terminfo ingestion path. Do not analyze untrusted terminfo during incident response.
assessment.upstream_remedy: ncurses upstream patch level 6.5-20251213; no fixed Trixie package recorded.

assessment.upstream_remedy: MariaDB Server 11.8.9 (other maintained branches also patched).

assessment.assessment: Health check uses explicit http://localhost/livez; build key download and GitHub issue submission use explicit HTTPS. No matching CLI options found. A libcurl package match alone does not establish the CLI vulnerability in PHP.

assessment.assessment: systemd-homed package is absent; Apache/CLI entrypoints do not start systemd as PID 1. Other systemd binary packages inherit the source advisory.

assessment.exploit_condition: Galera server has wsrep_notify_cmd enabled and accepts a malicious joiner name.
assessment.assessment: Affected server/backup component absent from the 200-package release inventory; Dockerfile installs clients only. No application-container exploit path established. This does not assess any external database server.

assessment.exploit_condition: Privileged libacl pathname-based operations process attacker-replaceable path components.
assessment.assessment: No KMP ACL API/setfacl path found; filesystem chown/mkdir are not automatically the affected ACL functions. Privileged worker/startup code still exists, so rootless/capability isolation must not be assumed.
assessment.upstream_remedy: acl 2.4.0; new *_at ABI requires callers and dependencies to be reviewed.

assessment.exploit_condition: Untrusted XML with an internal DTD reaches xmlParseInternalSubset.
assessment.assessment: libxml2 2.9.14 remains affected and PHP loads XML APIs. HTTP BodyParser leaves XML disabled, but Bootstrap Matching uses XMLReader on generated markup; report summaries parse HTML. No demonstrated attacker-controlled DTD path. NONET/default external-entity restrictions do not repair this memory bug.
assessment.upstream_remedy: Upstream fix 463bbeeca1805b5c4828f50d0fefc4eebaf620df (2.11.0); Debian fixed unstable from 2.14.5+dfsg-0.1. No fixed Trixie package.

assessment.exploit_condition: Python libxml2 SAX attributeDecl callback handles a DTD with enumerated attributes.
assessment.assessment: python3-libxml2 and Python runtime packages are absent from the release inventory; no Python step in the runtime recipe. This Python binding flaw is not demonstrated through PHP DOM/XMLReader.

assessment.exploit_condition: fstab-authorized external helper fails, then privileged X-mount post-hooks run.
assessment.assessment: No application mount invocation or configured fstab entries found in source/comparison image. Release filesystem not directly inspected. Proposed production chmod removes SUID/SGID from mount and umount, reducing the non-root escalation path. Root/capability-bearing callers remain privileged.
assessment.upstream_remedy: Upstream util-linux security fixes; advisory lists patched 2.41.6/2.42.3. Wait for a supported Trixie backport and verify actual code.

assessment.exploit_condition: A root/CAP_SYS_ADMIN operator uses nsenter --join-cgroup against an attacker-controlled target.
assessment.assessment: 2.41.5 includes the vulnerable option. It is not SUID and KMP does not invoke it, but a privileged operator can trigger the issue. Removing mount SUID does not mitigate this separate path.
assessment.upstream_remedy: Upstream advisory lists 2.41.6/2.42.3; Debian additionally references fix commit 286dd3ff41526b582ef48830de239dffbaa61f90 in 2.42.4. Require verified vendor backport.

assessment.exploit_condition: Linux >=6.15, X-mount.subdir, and a detached-tree fast path introduced in util-linux 2.42.
assessment.assessment: Installed 2.41.5 predates the upstream affected fast path. Debian still marks its source package affected. Treat this as a probable version exclusion until downstream source/backports are checked; no host-kernel version assumption. Proposed mount chmod adds defense in depth.
assessment.upstream_remedy: Upstream util-linux advisory/fix; confirm affected code rather than trusting the source-package match.

assessment.exploit_condition: An attacker replaces an fstab-authorized bind source; SUID mount applies owner/group/mode hooks to the wrong inode.
assessment.assessment: No application mount invocation or configured fstab entries found in source/comparison image. Release filesystem not directly inspected. Proposed production chmod removes SUID/SGID from mount and umount, reducing the non-root escalation path. Root/capability-bearing callers remain privileged.
assessment.upstream_remedy: Upstream util-linux security fixes; advisory lists patched 2.41.6/2.42.3. Wait for a supported Trixie backport and verify actual code.

assessment.exploit_condition: libcurl reuses Negotiate-authenticated connections across different service names.
assessment.assessment: No Negotiate/service-name options found in application clients; issue submitter uses a fresh HTTPS handle with explicit headers. Ordinary HTTPS use is not sufficient for this flaw.

assessment.exploit_condition: Server ST_AsText serializes a crafted deeply nested GeometryCollection.
assessment.assessment: Affected server/backup component absent from the 200-package release inventory; Dockerfile installs clients only. No application-container exploit path established. This does not assess any external database server.

assessment.exploit_condition: mariadb-dump or SHOW CREATE serializes malicious identifiers; a consumer subsequently executes the generated SQL.
assessment.assessment: The dump client IS installed; this is not a server-only false positive. KMP tenant backups use PHP JSON/gzip, platform backups use pg_dump/pg_restore. No application use of mariadb-dump/mysqldump found. Manual SQL dump/restore remains an operator risk.
assessment.upstream_remedy: MariaDB client/server 11.8.9. Do not replay SQL generated by an affected dump client from an untrusted database.

assessment.exploit_condition: Qualified-name dictionary sizing overflows while processing extremely large prefix/name data.
assessment.assessment: PHP DOM/XMLReader load this library. Generated markup and disabled raw XML requests reduce exposure; upstream patch adds allocation-size overflow checks. No triggering KMP input demonstrated. PHP memory/upload limits reduce opportunity but are not a bound on every native allocation.

assessment.exploit_condition: xmlURIEscapeStr processes an input beyond its integer-length range.
assessment.assessment: Upstream patch addresses xmlStrlen behavior for strings beyond INT_MAX; Debian says code was introduced in 2.13.0 yet marks really2.9.14 Trixie vulnerable. No such KMP input found. Possible version mismatch needs downstream source review, not an automatic false-positive closure.

assessment.exploit_condition: DTD validation error reporting reaches xmlSnprintfElements with an overflowing content model.
assessment.assessment: No application DTD validation call found; Bootstrap XMLReader uses default validation settings. The affected library remains loaded, so absence of an obvious validate() call is a reachability inference.

assessment.exploit_condition: An oversized XPointer expression reaches xmlXPtrEvalXPtrPart.
assessment.assessment: No XPointer/XInclude evaluation found in core, utility plugins or shipped Composer call sites. DOMXPath for fixed report selectors is not the XPointer API.

assessment.exploit_condition: Very large XML output causes a negative length to reach a write callback.
assessment.assessment: Grid summaries parse HTML and Bootstrap readInnerXML serializes generated fragments. No multi-gigabyte output or custom write callback found. Post-parse summary truncation does not constrain initial parsing/native allocations. Retain residual review.

assessment.exploit_condition: XInclude processing drops parser flags and a resource loader fetches an attacker-supplied include.
assessment.assessment: No XInclude calls or custom resource-loader registration found. The report loadHTML(..., LIBXML_NONET) call does not perform XInclude processing. NONET alone would not mitigate the advisory if XInclude were added.

assessment.exploit_condition: An X11 client uses XkbGetMap against a malicious X server.
assessment.assessment: libX11 is installed, but production is headless: no DISPLAY configuration, X11 socket mount, Xkb client call, ImageMagick or Ghostscript found in the runtime recipe/inventory. PDFs use bounded pure-PHP parsing and GD placeholders. Library presence is not proof of an X-server connection.
assessment.upstream_remedy: libX11 upstream fix 6d4432b13c0b3b6a644c13de9c793a14db48d545; advisory names 1.8.14, Debian has no fixed package yet.

assessment.assessment: Affected server/backup component absent from the 200-package release inventory; Dockerfile installs clients only. No application-container exploit path established. This does not assess any external database server.

assessment.exploit_condition: Perl Archive::Tar reads an unbounded attacker-controlled tar-entry size.

assessment.upstream_remedy: Archive::Tar 3.10; Debian defers pending upstream regression fixes.
